Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Daniel (Meridian CTO), Priya (Meridian ML), Sandeep (Meridian Infra), Lena (Meridian PM)

Summary:
- Goal: scope a 4-week pilot focused on integration and workload benchmarks to validate OpenAI-compatible API/gateway approach, SDK ergonomics, and structured output enforcement.
- Key criteria: p99 latency targets, throughput for peak windows, functional parity with OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and observability for cost/per-token breakdown.

Topics covered: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, SDK/gateway design, function/tool-calling, structured JSON outputs, security/network constraints, timeline and next steps.

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I think we have about 55, 56 minutes so we want to be pragmatic — quick intros and then jump into pilot scope.
[00:12] Daniel (Meridian): Yeah thanks, appreciate it. We got a couple folks on from infra and ML. We're trying to figure out how to replace our current OpenAI endpoints with something that gives us more predictable cost and control.
[00:23] Marcus (Redwood): Great context. We'll walk through the end-to-end plan: SDK integration, the gateway compatibility layer, and then the benchmark harness. I can run through the tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:35] Priya (Meridian): Quick note — our primary blockers are: data residency (can't send raw customer data to third parties in some flows), SSO/auth constraints, and hitting p99 latency under 1.2s for chat generation at our 99th percentile during peak.
[00:50] Sandeep (Meridian): And we have a 10% usage burst window every day at 16:00 local, so throughput is important. Also need to know if Redwood's SDKs support our internal gateway patterns.
[01:05] Aisha: Understood. For pilot success criteria, from what I heard: 1) functional parity with OpenAI-compatible API for your existing calls including function/tool calling; 2) p99 latency under 1.2s for the sampled prompt set; 3) cost per 1k tokens within the target band you guys set; 4) clear observability to explain regressions. Does that capture it?
[01:20] Lena (Meridian): Yes. Add: ability to enforce structured JSON responses for downstream parsers — we need schema enforcement.
[01:28] Marcus: Okay schema enforcement is doable two ways: 1) prompt engineering + evals, 2) native structured output feature in the SDK / response parser that validates and retries on schema mismatch. We'll prototype both.
[01:40] Daniel: Can you explain 'OpenAI-compatible' — we have an existing gateway that calls openai.com/v1 endpoints. We want minimal change.
[01:48] Marcus: Redwood offers a compatibility endpoint surface — same request/response shapes, same fields for function calling — so your gateway can swap the host header. SDKs also have a drop-in mode which maps the OpenAI names to Redwood API names. Small auth header change.
[02:05] Priya: Any gotchas around function/tool calling? We use tool calling to run SQL queries and perform structured lookups.
[02:12] Marcus: Key things: the function calling signature is preserved. We do suggestions for token budgeting and have hooks in the SDK that stream function call arguments so you can run tools server-side without leaking secrets. There's also a signed webhook pattern for tool callbacks.
[02:28] Sandeep: For private deployments, how does networking work? Do we need VPC peering or can we do a proxy?
[02:33] Aisha: For the pilot we typically use our hosted sandbox but we can also offer a VPC-enabled private plane if you need data stay-in-region. We'll confirm exact options in the security pack.
[02:45] Daniel: On benchmarks — what does the plan look like?
[02:48] Marcus: We propose a 2-week active benchmark window inside the 4-week pilot. Week 1: baseline runs against your sample traffic (lower concurrency) to calibrate model variants and quantization. Week 2: scaled stress tests including burst windows and p95/p99 tail latency capture. We'll run 3 model variants (base, quantized int8, and a smaller latency-optimized variant) and compare cost/latency/quality.
[03:12] Priya: How do you measure quality? Our tolerances are strict — we need structured output correctness > 98% on our golden set.
[03:19] Marcus: We'll run your golden set evals and produce an automated report. We also instrument hallucination detectors (heuristic checks) and will show diffed outputs per prompt.
[03:28] Lena: About workload sizing — our daily token volume is roughly 60M tokens/day, with peak QPS of about 380 requests/minute during the burst. Average request size is ~450 tokens.
[03:40] Marcus: Okay that's helpful. We'll map those numbers to concurrency and batching strategies. Batching can substantially reduce cost, but adds latency. For your p99 requirement we may limit batching on critical routes and enable it on async/low-latency-sensitive routes.
[03:55] Daniel: Can Redwood's runtime do prefix KV caching? We have repeatable prompts across sessions.
[03:59] Marcus: Yes, Redwood supports KV caching and prefix cache to reduce re-computation. We'll recommend a caching policy based on your prompt overlap profile.
[04:10] Aisha: Quick interjection — timeline recommendation: Week 0 (prep): exchange security docs, provision dev keys, set up sample data and SDK drop-in. Week 1-2: bench window. Week 3: integration work and structured output retries. Week 4: finalize report and decision gate.
[04:26] Priya: That timeline sounds reasonable. Can we get an itemized SOW and an estimated cost for the pilot?
[04:32] Aisha: Yes — we'll deliver SOW + pilot pricing. We typically bill flat for the pilot and include modest infra credits for the benchmark runs.
[04:40] Sandeep: Encryption — we use KMS, HSM for some keys. We need to know if Redwood can integrate with our KMS and ensure no plaintext storage in external logs.
[04:50] Marcus: For private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS and disable persisting logs. For hosted pilot, we'll provide options: redaction or customer-managed encryption for payloads. We'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[05:03] Daniel: Does the SDK allow streaming responses and partial function call arguments? We rely on server streaming to show progressive UI states.
[05:11] Marcus: Yes streaming is supported; we stream tokens as chunked responses and also partial function arguments so you can start executing tool steps earlier. There may be slight differences in chunk framing compared to OpenAI but we provide adapters in the SDK.
[05:25] Lena: On instrumentation — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards. Is that standard?
[05:31] Aisha: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route tokens, cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, and trace links. We'll give you a demo of console dashboards in the next meeting.
[05:40] Priya: For structured output enforcement, can the SDK validate JSON against a schema and automatically re-prompt?
[05:46] Marcus: Yes, we'll ship a validator that runs client-side: if the response fails schema validation, the SDK can either retry or run a small repair prompt. We log these incidents to the console so you can track failure modes.
[05:58] Daniel: About quality vs quantization — how do you recommend balancing cost and quality?
[06:03] Marcus: We'll present per-model quality scatter plots from the benchmark: BLEU-like and schema correctness rates vs cost/latency. For critical routes you may keep a higher-fidelity model, and route lower-priority traffic to quantized variants. Smart routing policies can do that automatically.
[06:20] Priya: Authentication: SSO/SAML integration for our internal users during the pilot?
[06:24] Aisha: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC for team-level access. For the pilot we'll provide single-user tokens for bench but can set up SAML for broader access if you want.
[06:35] Sandeep: Any typical pitfalls we should watch for during integration?
[06:38] Marcus: Common things: 1) mismatched tokenization assumptions, 2) function signature differences (we keep parity but check), 3) network egress rules blocking callbacks, 4) trusting prompt-engineered structured output without schema gating. We'll run preflight checks to catch these.
[06:55] Lena: What success gate do you expect at the end of 4 weeks?
[06:59] Aisha: A simple gate: if p99 latency <= 1.2s on priority routes AND structured output correctness >= 98% on your golden set AND cost per 1k tokens within agreed band, then we consider pilot successful and propose next steps for Dedicated or Private deployment.
[07:15] Daniel: Sounds good. Let's talk schedule: can we start next Monday with prep?
[07:20] Aisha: Yes, next Monday works. We'll send the SOW and a proposed calendar with the benchmark window slots.
[07:26] Priya: One more technical: do you run end-to-end tests with our database for tool calls? We prefer a stubbed environment for pilot.
[07:31] Marcus: We recommend a staging DB or a mock service for tool callbacks. We'll provide the harness to simulate latency and DB responses.
[07:40] Sandeep: For the benchmark harness, what metrics do you collect?
[07:44] Marcus: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, cost estimate per model/variant, schema validation failure rate, error distribution, and tail latency traces. We'll produce CSV/JSON outputs and a slide deck with recommendations.
[07:57] Lena: Any legal or procurement steps we should start now?
[08:02] Aisha: We'll attach a standard pilot agreement and data processing addendum. Procurement can review while we prep the technical pieces.
[08:10] Daniel: Okay let's recap.
[08:12] Aisha: Recap: Redwood will send SOW + pricing, security pack, benchmark harness, and sample SDK. Meridian will provide traffic profile, golden prompt sets, VPC constraints, and internal sign-off. We'll schedule the benchmark window and share meeting invites.
[08:30] Priya: Thanks. I think that's clear.
[08:33] Marcus: I'll follow up with the harness link and a quick README.
[08:36] Sandeep: I'll start documenting the network constraints.
[08:38] Daniel: Thanks all — excited to see the data.
[08:40] Aisha: Thanks everyone. We'll send action items and calendar invites after the call.
[08:45] [end of main conversation]
